criterion: A segment leaderboard renders as a real table with column headers and states each place in text rather than carrying the place only in colour.
evaluation_rule: The segment page is the page for one named stretch of road. Yes if the standings are a table with headers naming rank, athlete and time, and each row shows its place as a readable number or word. No if the standings are a styled list of rows, or if the first three places are distinguished only by a gold, silver or bronze colour with no place written anywhere.

criterion: The feed is a stream of activity cards, each carrying a route picture and a block of statistics rather than a bare line of text.
evaluation_rule: The feed is the signed-in page listing the activities of the athletes the viewer follows. Yes if each entry is a card showing who recorded it, a drawn route, and distance, time and climbing together. No if the feed is a list of names and dates with no drawn route and no grouped numbers.

criterion: The activity page states that the map is partial where a privacy zone cut the route short, and still reports the distance and time of the whole activity.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the activity page carries a visible note that part of the route is hidden, and the distance and time shown are those of the whole activity. No if the route simply starts somewhere odd with no explanation, or if the numbers shrink to match the drawn part.

criterion: The activity page reports segment matching as still in progress until the efforts appear.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the segment area of a freshly uploaded activity shows a working or pending state until its efforts appear. No if it shows a count of zero or an empty list while the work is still going on, which the athlete reads as a fact about their ride.

criterion: The upload route runs as an ordered set of steps, one decision at a time, and names the state the upload has reached as the state changes.
evaluation_rule: Yes if choosing the file, confirming the type and name, setting the visibility and submitting are separate steps with the current one named, and the page then shows the upload moving through its states on its own. No if the whole thing is one form, or if the athlete has to reload to learn what happened.

criterion: A suspected duplicate upload shows both candidates side by side with the numbers that tell them apart and asks the athlete which to keep.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the athlete is shown the existing activity and the new one together, with their start times, durations and distances, and a control to choose one. No if the duplicate is silently dropped, or if the athlete is told only that something was a duplicate with no way to decide.

criterion: One saturated orange carries the brand, and the first, second and third place colours are reserved for ranks and achievements.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the only strongly saturated hue in the interface is the brand orange, and the podium colours appear only beside ranks and medals. No if a second saturated hue competes with the brand, or if the first-place colour is reused as a general warning or highlight anywhere.

criterion: Numbers in leaderboards and statistic blocks line up in their columns because the digits are all the same width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the digits in a column of times or distances sit directly above one another and do not shift as values change. No if the numbers jiggle from row to row because the digits have different widths.

criterion: The signup landing is a three-panel composition whose form sits in a white column between two full-height panels, with the two federated controls above an emphasised email control.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the wide layout shows a panel, the form, and a panel, running to the edges of the window, with the two federated controls above the email control and only the email control filled in the brand colour. No if the form sits on a plain page, or if the branded control is a federated one.

criterion: An unrecorded statistic renders on the activity page as absent.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an activity recorded without a power meter or a heart-rate strap shows a dash, a blank or an explicit absence for that measurement. No if it shows a zero, which tells the athlete something false about their own ride.

criterion: On the upload route the loading indicator turns unevenly, speeding up and then easing, rather than rotating at one constant rate.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the indicator on the upload route accelerates through more than one full turn and then slows, reading like a wheel spun by hand. No if it turns at a constant rate like a machine.

criterion: The activity page carries the route as text giving distance, climbing and location, alongside the drawn map.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the activity page carries a readable summary of where the activity went and how far and how much it climbed, separate from the drawn route. No if the drawn route is the only carrier of that information, which excludes anybody using a screen reader from the product entirely.

criterion: A printed activity page carries the route, the summary statistics and the splits, leaving the feed chrome off the page.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a print preview of an activity shows its route, numbers and splits on the page without the header, footer and navigation. No if printing reproduces the whole screen, or if the route and the numbers are cut off.

criterion: A replay of a route begins moving across the map on its own when the activity page opens.
evaluation_rule: Yes if opening an activity starts an animated trace or a moving map without the reader asking for it. No if any replay waits for a play control, which is what it must do: an animated replay of a route is exactly the movement that makes some people ill.

criterion: A control reserved for subscribers is hidden from a free athlete's interface with its endpoint still answering that athlete.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a gated capability is kept away from a free athlete only by removing the control from the page, so calling the same address directly still works. No if the refusal comes from the server whether or not the control was ever shown.
